findings.text: The host memory-encryption mask setter records a value and mask for shadow entries. When the value carries bits outside the mask the implementation warns and clears both to zero, enforcing a subset relationship before publishing the globals.

The EPT mask initializer records whether accessed and dirty tracking is available and then publishes a family of shadow masks covering user, accessed, dirty, execute, supervisor-execute and present semantics plus access-track, host-writable and MMU-writable views, and programs an MMIO reserved pattern that avoids the write-plus-execute misconfiguration encoding.

Shadow EPT entries always derive their two execute controls from the paired access execution permissions regardless of host MBEC support. Non-nested mappings keep the pair together so the controls agree, and nested handling when L1 disables MBEC depends on presence logic skipping guest bit 10 and on permission tables omitting the user-execute permission. Hardware lacking MBEC safely ignores the extra control.

Two-bit accessed-dirty mode lives at the top of the shadow entry starting at bit 60 with encodings for fully enabled, fully disabled and write-protect-only operation, and a three-value mask selects that field.
Shadow paging uses nine bits per level with level shift and per-table entry count derived from that width, and the MMU-present indicator occupies bit 11.
The base address mask has two build variants, one intersecting the runtime physical mask with a page-aligned mask and one using a fixed 52-bit physical range intersected with a page-aligned mask.

Access-track save area preserves read and both execute controls shifted to start at bit 52. Default host-writable and MMU-writable indicators use bits 9 and 10, while EPT variants relocate them to bits 53 and 55.

MMIO generation number is split between a low field covering bits 3 through 9 and a high field covering bits 52 through 62, with derived widths, shifts and combined mask. Only top bit 63, address bits 51 to 12, bit 10 and low bits 2 to 0 may appear in an MMIO entry. Nonpresent value has two build variants, all-zero or top bit set, frozen state combines nonpresent with low pattern 0x1a0, and nonpresent-or-reserved mask length is five.

The TDP iterator object retains target and yielded guest frame numbers, an array of table pointers sized by maximum root level, current entry pointer and snapshot, lowest frame covered by current entry, address mask bits, root and minimum and current levels, address-space identifier, and valid and yielded flags. Path entries index by level minus one.

The walk begins validated at the requested root with frame rounded to that level. Advancing prefers descending one level when above the floor and the refreshed entry links a child, otherwise moves sideways within the table when not at the last slot, otherwise climbs until sideways progress is possible. Exhausting the root invalidates the walk, and a walk that yielded restarts from the root toward the recorded next frame instead of advancing.

Public walk operations comprise start with root, minimum level and frame targets, restart toward the recorded next frame, and advance to the next entry. Start rejects missing roots, out-of-range levels and inconsistent frame mask arguments by marking the iterator invalid.

Descending refreshes the current entry before following a child so that tables unlinked concurrently are not traversed. Sideways motion is barred at the final slot of a table and upward motion is barred at the root level.

Root selection requires the VM MMU lock held and additionally takes RCU read protection while scanning the TDP root list, acquiring a reference on the matching root and releasing the previous root reference before returning. The iteration macro asserts MMU lock and skips roots whose address-space identifier or type mask does not match.
Root type mask distinguishes invalid, direct and mirror roots, with combined sets for valid roots and for all roots.

Shadow-page reclamation runs as an RCU callback that warns on externally allocated tables before freeing. Role validity fields remain MMU-lock protected even though list linkage itself is RCU protected.
IO MSR filtering allows up to 256 entries. A range descriptor carries flags, count, base and bitmap pointer, and a filter object holds up to sixteen ranges plus a count and default-allow flag.
User-return MSR support allows up to sixteen slots with a global count and per-CPU array of host and current values plus registration state and notifier linkage.

Slot registration probes readability and writability with preemption disabled and only then appends the identifier. Online initialization snapshots host values into both stored copies. Masked updates preserve unselected host bits, skip redundant writes, attempt a safe write and arm the return-to-user notifier on success. The notifier restores diverged host values and unregisters, and explicit drop forces that restore path.

Exported user-return operations include destroy-all, add slot, per-CPU online snapshot, masked set, current-value query and forced restore, plus ignored-MSR toggles controlling whether unknown accesses fault and whether they are reported.

Index-list queries follow copy-in header, publish required count, fail with too-big when the caller buffer is short, then copy out the concatenated saved-plus-emulated list or the feature-only list. Separate routines serve the full list and the feature list.

Saved set combines a base architectural list covering system entry, timing, protection and tracing controls with a performance list covering fixed, architectural, legacy and AMD counters. Emulated set combines KVM paravirtual clocks and async controls, optional Hyper-V enlightenments, and architectural capability and VMX control identifiers. Feature set is a small subset plus the emulated VMX range.

Immutability holds for every identifier in the emulated VMX interval and for every member of the non-VMX feature base except the microcode revision. Advertisement holds when an identifier appears in either the saved array or the emulated array.

Unknown MSR handling can be globally downgraded from fault to ignore, with a separate toggle controlling whether such ignores are reported. Misconfiguration risks silently hiding guest reliance on unimplemented controls.
IO MSR transfer cap is 256 and user-return slot cap is 16, with MSR filter capacity fixed at 16 ranges.
Subsystem headers are protected by single-inclusion macros and translation units define a module-prefixed log format.
